title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 13

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the toolpath lesson begin?
tasks.audioText: The manufacturing lecturer will introduce toolpath terminology on Wednesday at nine thirty. Students should meet in the CNC theory room and bring the illustrated toolpath sheet. The lesson will compare a straight-line path with a curved path and identify the difference between the programmed geometry and the actual machine movement. The class will use diagrams only.

tasks.prompt: A toolpath describes the route followed by a cutting tool relative to a workpiece. In a simple example, a linear path connects two points with a straight movement, while a circular path follows an arc. The programmed path is interpreted by the controller, and the resulting movement depends on the machine configuration and settings. A drawing helps students visualise the geometry without operating equipment. Reading 1. What does a toolpath describe?
options: The route followed by a cutting tool relative to a workpiece

tasks.prompt: What can affect the resulting machine movement?
The programmed path ___ by the controller.
Choose TWO types of toolpath geometry.
A curved part of a circular toolpath is an ___.
A toolpath diagram is unclear. What should you ask?
options: I will assume the route is correct.
Could you explain how the programmed geometry is represented in this diagram?

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of toolpath concepts in a logical order.
options: Relate the path to the component drawing
Identify the start and end points
Describe the intended route using correct terms
correctOrder: Identify the start and end points

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining what a toolpath represents. Compare linear and circular path geometry at a conceptual level.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: toolpath is explained as the planned path/geometry represented by a programme (0–2); linear and circular path geometry are compared conceptually and accurately (0–2); the explanation is clear with understandable grammar (0–2); toolpath/geometry vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
